lessons.title: Story Time: A Toy from the Past
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make inferences about a character from a historical toy story.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about the story.
I can guess how a character feels.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of old-fashioned toys and predict the story.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story featuring an old-fashioned toy (e.g. a wooden toy, teddy bear), modelling inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer inference questions about how characters feel, using evidence from the text/pictures.
resources_needed: Story book featuring a historical toy
key_questions: How do you think the toy felt?

differentiation.support: Point to picture clues to answer
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain inference reasoning in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note inference skill development — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the story and inferences made.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member about a toy they had when they were young.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Numbers to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to read and write numbers to 20 in numerals and words.
success_criteria: I can read numbers to 20.
I can write numbers to 20 in words for some numbers.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting to 20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading and writing numbers 11-20 in numerals and words (eleven, twelve...).
lessons.independent_task: Children match numeral cards to word cards and practise writing some numbers in words.
key_questions: How do you write 'fourteen' in words?

differentiation.support: Focus on numbers to 12 with matching only
differentiation.greater_depth: Write numbers 13-20 in words independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record reading/writing of numbers to 20 — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire numeral/word matching game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading and writing numbers to 20 together.

lessons.title: What Toys Did Grandparents Play With?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a toy from the past and describe it.
success_criteria: I can name a toy from the past.
I can describe what it was made from.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap interviews about family toys from last week's home link.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce examples of toys from the past (spinning tops, wooden dolls, tin soldiers, hoops).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label a toy from the past they've learned about, describing its material.

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare the material to a modern equivalent toy

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall and description of historical toys — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap historical toys discussed.
lessons.home_link: Ask a grandparent or older relative about a toy they had.

lessons.title: Materials of Old Toys
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify materials commonly used in toys from the past.
success_criteria: I can name a material used in old toys.
I can compare it to a material used in modern toys.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap materials learned in Week 1 (wood, plastic, metal, fabric).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that many old toys were made from wood, tin and fabric, as plastic was less common.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort toy picture cards (old and new) by material and note which materials were more common in the past.
resources_needed: Old and new toy picture cards
key_questions: What material is this old toy made from?
Why might modern toys use more plastic?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why material use has changed over time

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of material change over time — evidence for SCI.MAT/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap materials used then and now.
lessons.home_link: Look at an old toy or photo of one and guess its material.

lessons.title: Writing About a Toy from the Past
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing a toy from the past using information gathered.
success_criteria: I can write a sentence about an old toy.
I can include what it was made from.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the toy from the past discussed on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about an old toy using gathered facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 1-2 sentences describing a toy from the past, checking punctuation.

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 3+ sentences with additional detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and factual recall — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write a sentence about the toy a family member told you about.

lessons.title: Sequencing Events in Time
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence events using time vocabulary (before, after, then).
success_criteria: I can order events using time words.
I can say what happened before/after.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sequencing words from earlier weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sequencing events on a simple timeline (e.g. grandparent's childhood, parent's childhood, now).
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence toy picture cards on a simple timeline from oldest to newest.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence 5+ items and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early chronological understanding — evidence for MATHS.MEA/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the timeline sequence created.
lessons.home_link: Create a simple timeline of your own toys from baby to now.

lessons.title: Using Photographs as Historical Evidence
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a photograph to find out information about the past.
success_criteria: I can look at a photo and say what I notice.
I can say what it tells us about toys in the past.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an old photograph of children playing (provided or found).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how photographs are a source of evidence about the past, modelling what to notice.
lessons.independent_task: Children examine an old photograph and record what they notice about toys/play in the past.
key_questions: What do you notice in this photo?
What does it tell us about toys then?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare to a modern photo and note differences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early historical enquiry skill using photographic evidence — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap what photographs can tell us about the past.
lessons.home_link: Look at an old family photo together and talk about what you notice.

lessons.title: Testing Toy Materials: Strength
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to test and compare the strength of different toy materials.
success_criteria: I can predict which material is strongest.
I can test my prediction safely.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict which material (wood, plastic, fabric) will be strongest.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a simple strength test (e.g. gentle bending/pulling) on material samples safely.
lessons.independent_task: Children test and record the strength of different material samples, comparing predictions to results.

differentiation.support: Test with adult support and simple recording
differentiation.greater_depth: Test 4+ materials and rank by strength with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note scientific enquiry skill: predicting and testing — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap which materials were strongest and why toys might use them.
lessons.home_link: Test the strength of two materials safely at home with an adult.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Old and New Toy Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words comparing old and new toys.
success_criteria: I can blend and read toy-themed words.
I can read a comparison sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap graphemes practised so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending words related to old/new toys.
lessons.independent_task: Children read word and sentence cards comparing old and new toys (e.g. 'the old toy is made of tin').
key_questions: Can you read this comparison sentence?

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Read comparison sentences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading old/new toy words over the week.

lessons.title: Solving Word Problems: Toys Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve simple addition/subtraction word problems using a toy context.
success_criteria: I can solve a simple word problem.
I can show my working using objects or drawings.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction from last week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a simple word problem using a toy context (e.g. 'there were 8 old toys, 3 broke, how many are left?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve 3-4 toy-themed word problems, showing their working.
key_questions: How will you work it out?

differentiation.support: Use counters and simplified numbers within 10
differentiation.greater_depth: Solve two-step word problems within 20

lessons.assessment_notes: Note problem-solving strategy and accuracy — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Recap strategies used to solve word problems.
lessons.home_link: Make up a simple toy word problem for your family to solve.

lessons.title: Museum Visit or Virtual Tour: Toys Through Time
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a toy from a different time period.
success_criteria: I can identify a toy from a museum resource.
I can say roughly when it might be from.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a museum is for.
lessons.main_teaching_input: (If possible) visit a local museum or explore a virtual museum toy collection resource, discussing exhibits.
lessons.independent_task: Children choose a toy artefact from the resource and record what it is and roughly when it's from.
resources_needed: Museum visit or virtual museum resource/pictures
key_questions: When do you think it's from?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare 2-3 artefacts from different time periods

lessons.assessment_notes: Note historical enquiry using museum-style resources — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite artefact discovered.
lessons.home_link: Look up an online museum toy collection together if possible.

lessons.title: Why Don't We Use Glass for Toys Anymore?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain a safety reason for material changes in toys.
success_criteria: I can say why glass isn't used for children's toys now.
I can suggest a safer material instead.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why some old toys used materials we wouldn't use now (glass, sharp metal).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss toy safety standards changing over time, linking to material choice.
lessons.independent_task: Children match unsafe old materials to safer modern alternatives, explaining why.
key_questions: Why isn't glass safe for toys?
What material could be used instead?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for 3+ material safety changes

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of material safety reasoning — evidence for SCI.MAT/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap why toy safety has improved over time.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a safety feature on one of your toys.

lessons.title: Spelling Toy-Themed Common Exception Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to spell common exception words in a toy-themed context.
success_criteria: I can spell 3 common exception words.
I can use one in a sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap common exception words learned so far (e.g. 'the', 'said', 'was').
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model spelling strategies for common exception words, using them in toy-themed sentences.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise spelling common exception words and use one in a toy-themed sentence.
key_questions: Can you use it in a sentence about a toy?

differentiation.greater_depth: Spell 5+ words and use multiple in a sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Record common exception word spelling progress — evidence for ENG.W1.
lessons.plenary: Quick spelling recap game.
lessons.home_link: Practise spelling common exception words together.

lessons.title: 3D Shapes: Toy Boxes and Blocks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and describe properties of common 3D shapes.
success_criteria: I can name a cube, cuboid, sphere and cylinder.
I can describe a property of each.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at toy boxes/blocks and discuss their shapes.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/recap 3D shape names using real toy boxes/building blocks as examples.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort toy-shaped objects by 3D shape name, recording properties (faces, edges).
key_questions: What 3D shape is this toy box?
How many faces does a cube have?

differentiation.support: Focus on cube and sphere only
differentiation.greater_depth: Include cone, pyramid and count edges/vertices

lessons.assessment_notes: Record 3D shape recognition and properties — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire 3D shape naming game.
lessons.home_link: Find 3D shaped toys/objects at home and name them.

lessons.title: Toys That Have Stayed the Same
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a toy that has remained similar over time.
success_criteria: I can name a toy that hasn't changed much.
I can explain why it might have stayed popular.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss teddy bears, dolls, or balls as examples that have existed for a long time.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why some toys (teddy bears, spinning tops, balls) have remained popular with little change.
lessons.independent_task: Children choose a 'classic' toy and explain why they think it has stayed popular.
key_questions: Why do you think it's stayed popular?

differentiation.support: Adult offers example choices with reasoning
differentiation.greater_depth: Give own reasoning independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reasoning about continuity over time — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap classic toys discussed.
lessons.home_link: Find a toy at home that might be similar to one from long ago.

lessons.title: Sorting Materials: Waterproof or Not?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to test whether a material is waterproof.
success_criteria: I can predict if a material is waterproof.
I can test it safely.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which materials might be waterproof (plastic vs fabric).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model testing material samples with a small amount of water to check if waterproof.
lessons.independent_task: Children test and record whether various material samples are waterproof.

differentiation.greater_depth: Test 5+ materials and rank by water resistance

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skills: testing and recording results — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap which materials were waterproof.
lessons.home_link: Test if a material at home is waterproof (with permission).

lessons.title: Comparing Two Toy Stories
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two stories about toys from different time periods.
success_criteria: I can say one similarity between the stories.
I can say one difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the story read on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a second toy-themed story (modern setting) and compare to Monday's historical one.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record one similarity and one difference between the two stories.
key_questions: What is similar about these stories?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative comprehension skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of similarities and differences found.
lessons.home_link: Compare two stories you know at home.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Numbers, Time, Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number, sequencing, and shape skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read/write numbers to 20.
I can sequence events.
I can name 3D shapes.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of numbers to 20, sequencing, and 3D shapes.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: number reading/writing, timeline sequencing, 3D shape sorting.
key_questions: What comes next in the sequence?

differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with extension challenges

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 3 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/MATHS.GEO/MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising numbers and shapes over the weekend.

lessons.title: Toys in the Past: Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about toys in the past learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a toy from the past.
I can describe what it was made from and how it's different from today.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's history learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about historical toys.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Toys in the Past' display combining drawings, photograph observations, and material comparisons from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about toys in the past?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain multiple ideas with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, ready to compare directly to modern toys next week — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Toys in the Past' display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about toys in the past with your family.

lessons.title: Science Review: Materials Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall material properties and testing methods learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a material property (strong, waterproof).
I can recall how we tested it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering material properties and testing from the week.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet on material properties and testing methods.
key_questions: What material property did we test?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain testing methods in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skills progress for the term — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's science learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned in science this week with your family.
